confidence_note: Global protein-family totals are not SCS-specific counts; annotations do not establish phosphorus flux for every host.

subject: src:scs-seep-dehalogenation
statement: Reductive-dehalogenase-like genes occurred across diverse archaeal and bacterial groups, with complementary chemical and experimental evidence supporting organohalide-transforming potential.
scope: Sixteen global seep sites, including Haima, Site F, Shenhu, and other SCS sites.
evidence_basis: RdhA-like sequence classification integrated with halogen chemistry, laboratory incubations, transcripts, and metabolomics.
locator: Abstract; Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets from cold seep sediments
confidence_note: RdhA-like annotation alone does not verify substrate specificity or field-scale remediation capacity.

subject: src:scs-seep-quorum-sensing
statement: Multiple signaling systems were detected across seep taxa, and representative LuxI–LuxR pairs showed activity in heterologous tests.
scope: Seventeen global seep sites including Haima, Site F, and other SCS regions.
evidence_basis: Quorum-sensing genes and transcripts compared with environmental gradients; representative LuxI–LuxR pairs tested by heterologous expression.
locator: Abstract; Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data processing
confidence_note: Presence and experimental function of selected signaling pairs do not demonstrate regulation of every inferred biogeochemical pathway in situ.

subject: src:scs-site-f-sponge-partitioning
statement: Sponge microbiomes had distinct composition, lower diversity, and enrichment of specialized sulfur- and methane-associated bacterial groups compared with environmental microbiomes.
scope: Site F sponge-associated, seawater, and sediment microbiomes.
evidence_basis: Six sponge species and environmental metagenomes compared using taxonomic profiles, MAGs, and functional annotations.
locator: Abstract; Sample and Data Collections
confidence_note: Different collection years confound direct habitat comparisons; functional gene abundance is not metabolic efficiency.

subject: src:scs-seep-defense-systems
statement: The comparative catalog revealed extensive defense and anti-defense diversity, and selected candidate microbial systems protected against viral infection in laboratory assays.
scope: Seventeen global seep sites; SCS sequences contribute to the comparative catalog.
evidence_basis: Microbial defense and viral anti-defense genes compared across genomes; selected candidate defenses experimentally tested.
locator: Abstract; Methods: Metagenomic datasets
confidence_note: Laboratory validation covers selected systems; co-occurrence does not establish synergism or infection rates in seep sediment.

subject: src:scs-site-f-water-spatial-2026
statement: Near-seep and deeper-water communities showed greater representation of methane- and sulfur-associated populations and genes, indicating spatially structured metabolic potential.
scope: Site F, near-seep sites and a station approximately 1 km away.
evidence_basis: Niskin bottles on CTD and ROV; 16S and metagenomic profiles compared across depth and distance.
locator: Abstract; Water Samples Collection and Pretreatment
confidence_note: Gene distributions do not quantify the fraction of vented methane removed during upward transport.

subject: src:scs-haima-domains-water-sediment-2026
statement: Microbial diversity and co-occurrence varied by compartment and habitat; modeled environmental selection differed between prokaryotes and microeukaryotes in water versus sediment.
scope: Haima water layers and mussel, anemone, bare seabed, dead-clam, and clam sediment habitats.
evidence_basis: CTD water profiles and ROV sediment cores to 30 cm; prokaryotic/microeukaryotic community and co-occurrence analyses.
locator: Abstract; Sample collection and measurement of environmental factors
confidence_note: Correlations and assembly models indicate ecological patterns, not demonstrated interspecies exchanges.

subject: src:scs-seep-nitrogen-methane-n2o
statement: Nitrate/nitrite-coupled methane oxidation had a larger potential contribution in early-stage than mature seep sediments, and nitrate/methane amendments increased net N2O production.
scope: Early-stage and mature South China Sea seep sediments.
evidence_basis: 14C labeling, omics, and gas-production analyses tested nitrate/nitrite-linked methane oxidation and N2O formation.
locator: Abstract; Sample collection and geochemical analysis
confidence_note: Potential rates and amendment responses cannot be treated as continuous natural emissions or global climate offsets.

subject: src:scs-newborn-seep-biofilter
statement: A methane-consuming animal–microbe assemblage developed within approximately one to two years at the monitored newborn seep, with aerobic and anaerobic methanotrophs and bioturbating fauna.

evidence_basis: More than 40 sites around the discharge center; ROV cores, porewater, molecular analyses, and in situ ecosystem observations.
locator: Abstract; Sediment and porewater sampling
confidence_note: One induced seep does not establish a universal recovery time or guaranteed mitigation of future methane releases.

subject: src:scs-haima-anme1-hotspots
statement: ANME-1 genomes contained variable hotspots associated with defense, transport, and methane-metabolism genes; heterologous hicAB tests supported toxin–antitoxin function.
scope: Haima sediment core at 1435 m water depth; four depth intervals within 30 cm.
evidence_basis: Long-read reconstruction of circular MAGs, genomic-hotspot comparisons, and heterologous tests of hicAB operons.
locator: Abstract; Sampling, DNA extraction, metagenomic library preparations and sequencing
confidence_note: One core and heterologous assays do not prove the drivers of speciation or stress responses in natural ANME populations.

subject: src:scs-haima-clam-sulfide-2026
statement: Moderate sulfide shortage preserved symbiont abundance, whereas severe shortage coincided with reduced abundance and altered host lysosomal pathways; sulfur-metabolism responses indicated symbiotic flexibility.
scope: Archivesica marissinica and sulfur-oxidizing symbionts at Haima, including HM-2 and HM-3.
evidence_basis: In situ clam transplantation with host/symbiont molecular profiling under moderate and severe sulfide shortage.
locator: Abstract
confidence_note: Molecular associations support a proposed buffering mechanism but do not directly measure symbiont carbon transfer or long-term resilience.

subject: src:scs-site-f-sponge-host-specificity
statement: The six sponge species hosted distinct bacterial assemblages, with SUP05 prominent in most samples.
scope: Six sponge species at the Formosa Ridge cold seep.
evidence_basis: Sixteen sponge samples analyzed with full-length 16S amplicons and bacterial phylogeny.
locator: Abstract; 2.1 Sample collection; 2.3 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and processing
confidence_note: Marker phylogeny does not measure sulfur/methane oxidation or establish the mechanism of host specificity.

subject: src:scs-haima-chondroitinase-a
statement: The recovered enzyme selectively cleaved chondroitin/dermatan sulfate motifs containing GalNAc or GalNAc4S; mutagenesis identified residues required for activity.

evidence_basis: Characterize a PL8 lyase using defined oligosaccharides, product analysis and site-directed mutagenesis.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Purified-enzyme specificity does not establish substrate availability, expression or turnover in seep sediments.

subject: src:scs-cross-latitude-carbon-fixation
statement: Incubated tropical sediments had higher dark carbon-fixation rates than subarctic sediments; carbon-fixation pathway inventories also differed between regions and depths.

confidence_note: Regional comparisons combine environmental and sampling differences; incubated rates are not annual in situ carbon budgets.

subject: src:scs-mussel-recovery-hours

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.

subject: src:scs-pressure-hydrocarbon-consortia

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Partner exchange is inferred from genomes, not directly measured; long enrichments select communities distinct from the initial sediment.

subject: src:scs-sitef-host-symbiont-connectivity

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.

subject: src:scs-haima-stenotrophomonas-wo2
statement: WO2 supplied a 4,772,190-bp draft genome with 66.01% GC content for investigating seep-derived hydrocarbon-utilizing bacteria.

evidence_basis: Isolate an oil-utilizing strain and assemble its draft genome.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: An isolate genome does not establish environmental abundance, substrate-specific rates or field remediation performance.

subject: src:scs-aom-dna-sip-partnerships

locator: Abstract; Sample collection and chemical analysis; SIP microcosms incubations for identification of microbes involved in the AOM.
confidence_note: Inhibitor effects and isotope incorporation require treatment-specific interpretation; laboratory redundancy is not a measured ecosystem resilience rate.

subject: src:scs-aspergillus-anthraquinones
statement: New anthraquinone-related metabolites were characterized; one assayed compound inhibited HT29 proliferation and colony growth in vitro.

evidence_basis: Purify metabolites, determine structures by NMR and mass spectrometry, and assay tumor-cell proliferation.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Cell-line activity is neither a clinical efficacy result nor evidence of the compounds' ecological role at seeps.

subject: src:scs-salegentibacter-two-species
statement: The two facultatively anaerobic isolates met the study's criteria for Salegentibacter profundi and S. haimaensis, with distinct tested growth ranges.

evidence_basis: Combine growth phenotypes, chemotaxonomy, phylogenomics and genome similarity comparisons.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Culture growth ranges describe these isolates and do not establish abundance or ecological dominance in situ.

subject: src:scs-haima-plastic-enrichments
statement: Plastic-associated enrichments grew and altered film surfaces; abundance changes identified candidate degraders, with candidate signals more abundant in seawater than sediment.

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Candidate ASVs and surface damage do not individually prove polymer mineralization or quantify natural removal rates.

subject: src:scs-haima-halogen-redox-profile
statement: The study detected 669 halogenated molecular formulas; organochlorine signals declined near a redox boundary and covaried with chemistry and dehalogenase inventories.

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Formula-level assignments do not resolve every chemical structure; correlations cannot separate microbial removal from burial and transport.

subject: src:scs-haima-alkane-methanogens

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Acetate accumulation and pathway genes do not directly trace alkane carbon into methane or prove the proposed syntrophic exchange.

subject: src:scs-haima-horizontal-assembly
statement: The seepage habitat had lower alpha diversity and distinct archaeal composition; modeled bacterial and archaeal assembly differed across habitats.

evidence_basis: Measure sediment geochemistry and 16S composition; estimate assembly and co-occurrence patterns.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Assembly models and co-occurrence edges describe statistical patterns, not demonstrated microbial interactions or causal environmental controls.

subject: src:scs-haima-amino-compounds

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Source fractions depend on biomarker assumptions; the profiles do not directly measure fungal biomass production or AOM-driven degradation rates.

subject: src:scs-haima-lignin-metabolism

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Genetic methylotrophic potential is not measured methane production, and enrichment turnover cannot establish a regional carbon sink.

subject: src:scs-lysinibacillus-wb86-genome

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.

subject: src:scs-scs-biosynthetic-survey

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Amplicon-based cluster estimates and metagenomic predictions require chemical or expression validation before claims of product synthesis.

subject: src:scs-haima-depth-assembly

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.

subject: src:scs-haima-viral-stages

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.

subject: src:scs-bacillus-haimaensis-resource

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Source assignments depend on isotope endmembers; carbonate storage cannot directly establish the global dissolved-black-carbon flux.

subject: src:scs-shallow-mussel-seep-transplant
statement: Exposed mussels acquired a microbiome richer in methanotrophs alongside host stress, immune and metabolic transcriptional changes.

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.

subject: src:scs-haima-microplastic-community-response

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Network fragility and predicted functions are not measured ecosystem instability, pathogen risk or in situ nutrient fluxes.

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.

subject: src:scs-yungan-tubeworm-microbes
statement: The trunk library contained one dominant symbiont phylotype; surrounding habitats included ANME-1b and abundant sulfur-oxidizing lineages.

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.

subject: src:scs-haima-plastic-aging

subject: src:scs-pacbio-shortread-sediment-comparison

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.

subject: src:scs-haima-dom-water-enrichment

locator: Abstract; Sample collection; DOM enrichment experiments.

subject: src:scs-effluviviacota-seep-genomes
statement: Effluviviacota genomes encoded fermentative carbohydrate/peptide use and candidate extracellular electron-transfer systems, with differences among genera.

subject: src:scs-fontisubflavum-water-isolate

subject: src:scs-remirge-functional-phylogeny

subject: src:scs-haima-minerals-microbes

locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.

subject: src:scs-abyssisolibacter-m8s5

subject: src:scs-haima-faunal-cs-cycling

subject: src:scs-haima-microeukaryotic-diversity

subject: src:scs-haima-sulfur-dom

subject: src:scs-scs-aom-biogeography

subject: src:scs-extinct-haima-metabolism
statement: The extinct seep retained distinctive bacterial assemblages and diverse carbon, nitrogen and sulfur metabolic potential despite cessation of visible seep activity.

subject: src:scs-srb-zero-valent-sulfur

subject: src:scs-sitef-horizontal-vertical-sediment

subject: src:scs-haiyang4-tetraether-lipids

evidence_basis: Analyze intact-polar and core GDGT fractions separately along the sediment profile.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Lipid-source assignments and preservation differ among fractions; ratios are not direct measurements of living biomass or metabolic rates.

subject: src:scs-bivalve-lipid-nutrition
statement: Methanotroph-hosting and thiotroph-hosting bivalves had distinct lipid signatures; matching host/symbiont isotope patterns supported substantial symbiont-derived nutrition.
scope: Four mussel/clam species from Site F and Haima.
evidence_basis: Analyze tissue lipids and compound-specific carbon isotopes to compare nutritional sources.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Biomarkers infer source contributions; they do not directly measure contemporaneous carbon-transfer rates or ambient oxygen.

subject: src:scs-scs-six-carbon-fixation-pathways
statement: Genes representing six carbon-fixation pathways were detected; rTCA was widespread and Wood–Ljungdahl pathway genes were concentrated in seep sediments.
scope: Sediments from two SCS cold seeps and one trough.
evidence_basis: Reconstruct carbon-fixation pathways from metagenomes and MAGs across sediment depths.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Gene presence and completeness do not establish pathway direction, expression or quantitative carbon-fixation contribution.

subject: src:scs-scs-microeukaryote-biogeography
statement: SAR lineages dominated; seep communities differed from the trough and contained many lineages related to parasitic or symbiotic taxa.
scope: Two northern SCS cold seeps and one trough.
evidence_basis: Use 18S amplicons and network analysis to compare microbial eukaryote composition.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Sequence affiliation and network correlations cannot identify actual trophic relationships or distinguish living cells from deposited DNA.

subject: src:scs-formosa-betaine-methanogenesis
statement: A bacterial–archaeal coculture converted glycine betaine to methane; dimethylglycine addition was required for the tested 4°C coculture.
scope: Formosa seep sediment and isolated Oceanirhabdus/Methanococcoides strains.
evidence_basis: Combine substrate amendments, inhibition, metagenomics, strain isolation and defined cocultures at 18°C and 4°C.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: The demonstrated route does not establish glycine betaine as the dominant methane precursor throughout natural seep sediments.

subject: src:scs-mussel-sulfide-detoxification
statement: Seep–vent differences and sulfide exposure involved host and symbiont sulfur-oxidation transcripts, including sqr, consistent with multiple detoxification components.
scope: Gigantidas platifrons from Formosa Ridge and Iheya North Knoll.
evidence_basis: Compare 16S and host/microbial transcription, then test mussel responses to Na2S exposure.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Transcriptional responses do not independently quantify detoxification flux or prove each partner's necessity.

subject: src:scs-acpsf1-archaeal-marker
statement: aCPSF1 clustering broadly agreed with established archaeal phylogenies and gave finer lower-rank resolution; the seep comparison produced similar diversity patterns.
scope: Global archaeal genomes and an SCS cold-seep sample used for marker comparison.
evidence_basis: Compare aCPSF1 phylogeny against 16S and phylogenomics, including a matched environmental diversity survey.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: One environmental validation does not establish universal primer coverage or equivalent quantitative abundance across archaeal lineages.

subject: src:scs-haima-methane-derived-doc
statement: Seep porewater had high DOC and strongly depleted carbon isotopes, together with more protein-like fluorescence, supporting a methane-related DOC contribution.
scope: Two Haima seep cores and a nearby reference core.
evidence_basis: Measure sulfate, DOC concentration, DOC carbon isotopes and fluorescence components.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Isotope/fluorescence proxies do not directly quantify methane-to-DOC production, microbial uptake or export into the ocean.

subject: src:scs-iocasia-carbohydrate-fermentation
statement: NS-1 used multiple tested carbohydrates and produced hydrogen and organic fermentation products, providing a cultivable model of seep carbohydrate processing.
scope: Iocasia fonsfrigidae NS-1 from an SCS deep-sea cold seep.
evidence_basis: Combine isolate taxonomy, carbohydrate growth tests, fermentation-product measurements and transcript analyses.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Isolate products do not establish partner uptake or the organism's contribution to natural seep carbon turnover.

subject: src:scs-psychrosphaera-ytuae
statement: The proposed Psychrosphaera ytuae grew from 4–40°C under tested conditions and carried a 3.33-Mb chromosome.
scope: Aerobic sediment strain MTZ26T from an SCS cold seep.
evidence_basis: Combine physiological and chemical traits with phylogeny and isolate genome analysis.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Laboratory temperature tolerance does not demonstrate in situ pressure adaptation or environmental abundance.

subject: src:scs-bacillus-fonticola
statement: Phenotypic and phylogenetic evidence supported Bacillus fonticola; tested growth occurred at 16–37°C and 0–8% NaCl.
scope: Sediment strain CS13T from an SCS deep-sea seep.
evidence_basis: Compare 16S phylogeny, growth ranges and cellular chemistry.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Culture-range observations cannot be used as ambient seep temperature/salinity or as evidence of ecological dominance.

subject: src:scs-shenhu-aom-without-anme
statement: Incubations showed methane oxidation and production despite no detected classical ANME sequences in the sampled sediments.
scope: Two Shenhu cores above the sulfate–methane transition zone.
evidence_basis: Combine geochemical profiles, high-throughput community sequencing and AOM/methanogenesis incubations.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: A non-detection is method dependent; the responsible organisms were unresolved and cannot be assigned to Bathyarchaeota from abundance alone.

subject: src:scs-artificial-seep-biocoenosis
statement: Bacteria and archaea colonized before observed jellyfish and amphipods; viruses were also detected in the constructed community.
scope: Methane-seeping device on the SCS seafloor at approximately 1,000-m depth.
evidence_basis: Deploy a methane biocoenosis generator and observe microbial and animal colonization.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Colonization succession does not directly trace electron or carbon transfer through all organisms or reproduce all natural seep conditions.

subject: src:scs-haima-bivalve-gill-markers
statement: Both hosts were dominated by Gammaproteobacteria but differed in bacterial diversity and composition, with distinct predicted functional profiles.
scope: Gigantidas haimaensis and Archivesica marissinica from Haima.
evidence_basis: Compare gill 16S communities and FAPROTAX/PICRUSt inferred functions.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: 16S-derived function prediction is not a metagenome, transcriptome or demonstrated chemoautotrophic nutritional pathway.

subject: src:scs-methanofollis-fontis-isolate
statement: The proposed Methanofollis fontis used formate or H2/CO2, whereas tested acetate, alcohol and methylamine substrates did not support methanogenesis.
scope: FWC-SCC2T from station C5-6 near Four-Way Closure Ridge seep.
evidence_basis: Test methanogenic substrates and compare physiology, 16S and genome similarity.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: A mesophilic isolate from nearby sediment cannot establish methane production at the active vent or its quantitative field contribution.

subject: src:scs-scs-n-damo-potential
statement: Methylomirabilis/Methanoperedens signals and related genes supported potential nitrate/nitrite-linked methane oxidation in some sampled habitats.
scope: Site F, Haima and Xisha trough reduced sediments.
evidence_basis: Compare microbial taxa and methane/nitrogen pathway genes across habitats.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: This study inferred potential from metagenomes; isotope-rate measurements are required to establish pathway contributions to methane removal.

subject: src:scs-nitrincola-iocasae
statement: A 4.17-Mb genome and polyphasic evidence supported Nitrincola iocasae as a distinct species.
scope: Facultatively anaerobic KXZD1103T from Formosa Ridge sediment.
evidence_basis: Combine physiology, 16S phylogeny, genome sequencing and relatedness comparisons.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Genus identity does not demonstrate nitrification, denitrification or a community-wide nitrogen-cycling role.

subject: src:scs-carbonate-phosphorus-speciation
statement: Calcium-bound P was the largest fraction; spatial and elemental associations supported multiple mineral and organic P retention pathways.
scope: Three SCS/East China Sea deep-sea seep carbonate sites.
evidence_basis: Measure phosphorus fractions and map P, Ca, C and Fe distributions with NanoSIMS/SEM.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: P–Fe covariation does not itself prove iron-dependent AOM as the dissolved-P source or quantify P flux.

subject: src:scs-erythrobacter-thiosulfate-pathway
statement: The tested bacterium converted thiosulfate to zero-valent sulfur through TsdA/SoxB-associated steps, with Sdo proteins involved in further oxidation.
scope: SCS cold-seep isolate Erythrobacter flavus 21-3.
evidence_basis: Combine sulfur-product identification, proteomics, genetic tests and intermediate stoichiometry.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Homolog distributions indicate possible capacity but cannot quantify this pathway's natural or global sulfur contribution.

subject: src:scs-formosa-sulfurovum-interface
statement: Sulfurovum dominated sampled interface communities; a reconstructed genome supported rTCA carbon fixation, sulfur oxidation and nitrate-utilization potential.
scope: Formosa near-seep water, surface sediment and Shinkaia gills.
evidence_basis: Combine short/full-length 16S amplicons and metagenomic binning across interface samples.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: A dominant marker lineage is not a cultured species or a demonstrated carbon/sulfur/nitrogen process rate.

subject: src:scs-jiaolong-vertical-prokaryotes
statement: Surface layers favored sulfur oxidizers and ANME-1, whereas deeper layers favored sulfate reducers and ANME-1/2; sulfur/nitrate genes covaried near the surface.
scope: Jiaolong sediments, comparing 0–6 and 8–14 cm layers.
evidence_basis: Pair 16S pyrosequencing with methane/sulfur/nitrate functional genes in metagenomes.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Gene co-distribution does not directly establish electron-acceptor coupling or partner-specific syntrophy.

subject: src:scs-mussel-methane-maintenance
statement: Symbiont abundance declined during maintenance; decline was greater without methane at days 24 and 34.
scope: SCS Bathymodiolus platifrons and its gill methanotrophic symbionts.
evidence_basis: Identify pmoABC, quantify symbiont marker DNA and verify abundance changes by microscopy.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Marker-DNA abundance and laboratory methane supply do not quantify native symbiont carbon fixation or transfer to the host.

subject: src:scs-global-seep-diazotroph-genomes
statement: Nitrogenase genes occurred across more archaeal/bacterial lineages and energy metabolisms than ANME–SRB alone, expanding the genomic catalogue of potential seep diazotrophs.
scope: Eleven global seep regions, including Jiaolong, Haiyang 4, Site F and Haima in the SCS.
evidence_basis: Analyze 61 metagenomes, 1,428 MAGs and six metatranscriptomes for nitrogenases and associated energy pathways.
locator: Abstract; Metagenomic datasets for deep-sea cold seep sediments; Introduction describing dataset composition.
confidence_note: Gene/transcript evidence does not establish fixation rates for every lineage or a quantitative global nitrogen budget.

subject: src:scs-scs-dna-rna-viral-carbon
statement: Nascent-seep viral communities differed from other habitats, including more RNA/temperate-virus signals; viral metabolic genes showed transcription consistent with possible organic-matter functions.
scope: Four SCS locations: declining seep, distant reference, nascent seep and seamount; uppermost 1-cm sediment.
evidence_basis: Combine purified viral fractions, DNA/RNA viromes, metagenomes and metatranscriptomes across contrasting habitats.
locator: Abstract; Sample collection and total organic carbon measurement; Results on the four-site comparison.
confidence_note: RNA detection and gene expression do not quantify infection rates or community carbon turnover; location and habitat effects overlap.

subject: src:scs-sitef-mussel-phage-expression
statement: Viral profiles differed among methane habitats; expressed phage contigs and shared gene signatures supported candidate associations with the gill symbionts.
scope: Nine Site F Gigantidas platifrons individuals, three each from high-, moderate- and low-methane habitats.
evidence_basis: Compare gill DNA/RNA viral profiles and infer phage links to methanotrophic symbionts.
locator: Abstract; Sample collection; Relative abundance and composition of viruses of G. platifrons.
confidence_note: Computational links and transcripts do not prove productive infection, horizontal transfer or a nutritional effect on the mussel.

subject: src:scs-twilight-particle-size-microbiomes
statement: Particle size and depth were associated with distinct communities and carbohydrate-degradation gene inventories; smaller fractions had lower diversity but more carbon-degradation genes.
scope: Haima/Site F water and SEATS comparison, plus Longqi vent; surface, approximately 200 and 800 m.
evidence_basis: Filter approximately 500 L per sample in situ into >50, 10–50 and 1–10 μm particle fractions; analyze metagenomes and carbon chemistry.
locator: Abstract; Sample collection, genomic DNA extraction, and sequencing; Chemical analysis of the seawater samples.
confidence_note: The sampled fractions are particle-associated, not all free-living microbes; gene inventories cannot quantify particle sinking or remineralization rates.

subject: src:scs-jiulong-uncultivated-lineages
statement: Nine phyla included uncultivated archaeal/bacterial lineages with carbon-fixation, organic-substrate use and nutrient-reduction potential; several pathway genes were transcribed.
scope: A core near Jiulong methane reef at 1,100-m water depth in northern SCS.
evidence_basis: Recover eleven >85%-complete genomes and inspect pathway genes and transcript support.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Transcription is stronger evidence than gene presence but does not establish complete pathway activity, partner exchange or flux.

subject: src:scs-carbonate-fossil-microbial-genomes
statement: Carbonates preserved ANME and aerobic ammonia-oxidizer signals with community composition distinct from sediment; degradation differed among samples.
scope: SCS and Gulf of Mexico seep carbonates.
evidence_basis: Extract carbonate metagenomes, reconstruct marker profiles and recover ten dominant prokaryotic genomes.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Preserved DNA and genomes do not establish viable cells or current microbial activity in the carbonate.

subject: src:scs-haima-organotrophic-chitin
statement: Many prevalent MAGs encoded organic-substrate use and elemental-cycling genes; a selected chitinase retained structure and showed enhanced activity under the tested pressure/temperature.
scope: Haima sediment microbiomes from active and extinct habitats.
evidence_basis: Analyze 225 nonredundant MAGs and test a candidate chitinase under 15-MPa, 4°C conditions.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: A selected enzyme assay cannot determine community chitin turnover or establish chitin as a long-term carbon/nitrogen store.

subject: src:scs-haima-arsenic-methane
statement: Seep arsenic enrichment was mainly sulfide bound; methane-related geochemistry and co-occurring arrA/dsrA genes supported linked arsenic–sulfur–methane potential.
scope: Haima seep sediments and porewater.
evidence_basis: Analyze arsenic binding forms, methane-oxidation proxies and arsenic/methane/sulfur genes.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Proxy correlations and genomic co-occurrence do not directly quantify coupled reactions; annual sequestration estimates depend on scaling assumptions.

subject: src:scs-haima-deep-core-community
statement: Microbial diversity declined with sediment depth and composition changed around geochemical transitions, including the approximately 70-cm interval.
scope: Haima methane-seep sediment profile extending to 290 cm.
evidence_basis: Compare 21 stratified samples using sediment chemistry, 16S profiles and ecological assembly models.
locator: Abstract; Introduction describing 21 stratified samples; Results: Microbial community structure at different depths.
confidence_note: Assembly-model assignments do not establish causal drivers; gene-based predictions are distinct from measured methane or sulfur rates.

subject: src:scs-curvularia-genome-led-metabolites
statement: Culture manipulation yielded six previously undescribed cytochalasans; selected compounds showed antimicrobial or seedling-radicle inhibition in laboratory tests.
scope: Curvularia verruculosa CS-129 from internal Shinkaia crosnieri tissue at an SCS seep.
evidence_basis: Use genome-guided culture changes, metabolite purification, structure determination and antimicrobial/seedling assays.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Culture-induced products and test-organism inhibition do not establish natural production, host protection or ecological function.

subject: src:scs-alternaria-wood-meroterpenoids
statement: Three new meroterpenoids were characterized alongside known congeners; selected products inhibited the tested Klebsiella and resistant Staphylococcus strains.
scope: Alternaria alstroemeriae CS-745 isolated from sunken logs at an SCS seep.
evidence_basis: Purify cultured metabolites, resolve structures/configurations and measure bacterial inhibition.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: In vitro inhibition does not demonstrate antibiotic efficacy in animals or an antimicrobial role in the seep wood habitat.

subject: src:scs-aspergillus-subversicolor-phenols
statement: New phenol derivatives were characterized, but the reported screening found no obvious activity in the tested assays.
scope: Haima-derived Aspergillus subversicolor CYH-17.
evidence_basis: Determine metabolite structures and test enzyme inhibition, antioxidant and antibacterial activity.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Negative screening applies to the stated assays and concentrations; chemical novelty alone does not imply useful biological activity.

subject: src:scs-aspergillus-fumitremorgin
statement: A new fumitremorgin-related derivative was reported; selected other isolated compounds showed antibacterial or enzyme-inhibitory activity.
scope: Haima-derived Aspergillus fumigatus CYH-5 cultures.
evidence_basis: Isolate a new derivative and known compounds, resolve structures and assay bacterial/enzyme inhibition.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Activity cannot be attributed to the new derivative when demonstrated for other compounds; source origin does not establish field metabolite production.

subject: src:scs-trichoderma-lipids-terpenoids
statement: Five new lipids and two known terpenoids were identified; selected compounds inhibited the tested wheat-pathogenic fungi.
scope: Trichoderma lixii R22 from SCS cold-seep sediments.
evidence_basis: Purify lipids/terpenoids, determine structures and test wheat-pathogen inhibition and brine-shrimp toxicity.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Laboratory pathogen inhibition does not establish agricultural field efficacy or cold-seep antifungal interactions.

subject: src:scs-talaromyces-saha-metabolites
statement: SAHA-treated cultures yielded seven new highly oxygenated products and altered metabolite profiles; one selected azaphilone inhibited tested agricultural fungi.
scope: Talaromyces minioluteus CS-113 from SCS seep sediments.
evidence_basis: Apply an HDAC inhibitor during culture, compare LC-MS products, determine structures and test fungal inhibition.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: A metabolite increase does not prove which silent gene cluster was activated or establish natural seep production.

subject: src:scs-talaromyces-inflammatory-assays
statement: A new alkaloid and known compounds were isolated; several products inhibited NO signals, and a selected compound altered LPS-associated cytokine responses.
scope: SCS seep-derived Talaromyces helicus SCSIO41311.
evidence_basis: Identify alkaloids and assay nitric-oxide inhibition and selected cytokine responses.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Cellular anti-inflammatory signals do not establish clinical benefit or a natural seep microbial function.

subject: src:scs-curvularia-cytochalasin-2022
statement: Two new cytochalasin derivatives and a newly reported natural product were characterized from the cultured fungus.
scope: Curvularia verruculosa CS-129 from Shinkaia crosnieri in an SCS seep.
evidence_basis: Isolate cytochalasin derivatives, resolve structures and screen antibacterial activity.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: The inspected abstract lists antibacterial testing but does not support compound-specific potency claims for all products.

subject: src:scs-penicillium-verrucosidins
statement: Six new verrucosidin derivatives were characterized and exhibited activity against selected test pathogens, with reported MICs of 4–32 μg/mL.
scope: Penicillium polonicum CS-252 from SCS seep sediment at 1,183-m water depth.
evidence_basis: Determine metabolite structures/configurations and test inhibition of selected human/aquatic pathogens.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Assay-specific MICs do not establish clinical efficacy, broad safety or the products' role in natural seep communities.

subject: src:scs-curvularia-cytochalasin-2021
statement: New cytochalasin structures included a thioether-linked dimer; selected compounds showed antibacterial or tumor-cell cytotoxicity in vitro.
scope: Curvularia verruculosa CS-129 from internal Shinkaia tissue in the SCS.
evidence_basis: Purify products, determine structures with spectroscopy/crystallography and measure bacterial or cell-line inhibition.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Different compounds produced different assay effects; the results do not demonstrate host protection or clinical utility.

subject: src:scs-eps364-bacterial-polysaccharide
statement: A phosphorylated, β-linked polysaccharide was characterized and altered Huh7.5 cell growth, adhesion and apoptosis-related responses.
scope: Vibrio alginolyticus 364 isolated from an SCS cold seep.
evidence_basis: Purify EPS364, characterize sugar composition and test cancer-cell responses with proteomic/qPCR analyses.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Cell-line effects do not establish a therapeutic benefit or an environmental biofilm function for EPS364.

subject: src:scs-bacillus-n11-polysaccharide-genome
statement: The isolate had a 4,497,340-bp circular genome containing candidate polysaccharide-degradation genes.
scope: Bacillus N1-1 isolated from an SCS cold seep.
evidence_basis: Sequence the complete genome of an isolate reported to degrade κ-selenocarrageenan.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Genome annotation does not identify the responsible enzyme or demonstrate natural occurrence and turnover of this modified substrate at seeps.

subject: src:scs-qiongdongnan-black-carbon-core
statement: Strong isotope depletion supported a methane-related black-carbon component, estimated at 31–43% of sedimentary black carbon during the reconstructed active period.
scope: Qiongdongnan Basin sediment cores with century-scale seep records.
evidence_basis: Combine black-carbon/organic-carbon isotopes, sediment chronology and source/burial scaling.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Microbial attribution and global burial estimates depend on endmembers, chronology and seep-area scaling; no global production rate was directly measured.

subject: src:scs-seep-magnetotactic-bacteria
statement: Magnetotactic bacterial signals were diverse and widespread in seep datasets; genomes suggested iron/sulfur metabolism potentially associated with methane cycling.
scope: Two active SCS seep sediments plus globally compiled seep metagenomes.
evidence_basis: Combine metagenomics, magnetic measurements and microscopy with genome-scale metabolic reconstruction.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Metabolic reconstructions do not demonstrate methane oxidation by magnetotactic bacteria or quantify their iron/sulfur fluxes.

subject: src:scs-methanochimaera-problematica
statement: The proposed Methanochimaera problematica used H2/CO2 or formate for methane production and required yeast extract under tested culture conditions.
scope: FWC-SCC4T from Four-Way Closure Ridge sediment offshore southwest Taiwan.
evidence_basis: Test substrates/growth and compare 16S, ribosomal-protein phylogeny and genome relatedness.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Laboratory nutrient requirements and mesophilic growth cannot determine native abundance or methane production at low seabed temperature.

subject: src:scs-shenhu-long-term-incubation
statement: Methane transformations persisted despite undetected classical ANME and declining SEEP-SRB1; community shifts left the responsible unconventional lineages unresolved.
scope: Shenhu sediment incubations with electron-acceptor treatments.
evidence_basis: Compare methane oxidation/production, sulfate/iron reduction and 16S community shifts during long enrichments.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Long incubation selects populations; co-enrichment cannot attribute AOM to Bathyarchaeota or prove iron-coupled pathways without targeted validation.

subject: src:scs-jiaolong-anme-metabolic-diversity
statement: ANME genomes contained methane/carbon pathways and candidate organic-carbon biosynthesis routes, including a transcriptionally supported propanoate pathway.
scope: Thirteen ANME draft genomes from Jiaolong cold seep.
evidence_basis: Compare five ANME types using MAG metabolic reconstruction and pathway transcript evidence.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Draft-genome gene absence is not definitive loss; predicted secretion and pathway transcription do not quantify metabolite release.

subject: src:scs-aequorivita-iocasae
statement: The facultatively anaerobic strain represented Aequorivita iocasae and grew optimally at 3–6% NaCl under tested conditions.
scope: KX20305T from SCS cold-seep sediment.
evidence_basis: Compare physiological/chemical traits, 16S and a 3.35-Mb isolate genome.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Culture optima are not measurements of natural seep salinity and do not establish an elemental-cycling role.

subject: src:scs-marinobacter-fonticola
statement: Evidence supported Marinobacter fonticola; tested growth spanned 4–40°C, pH 5–11 and 0–19% NaCl.
scope: CS412T isolated from an SCS cold-seep sediment.
evidence_basis: Combine 16S phylogeny, growth ranges and cellular chemical characteristics.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Wide culture tolerance does not establish dominance at seeps or hydrocarbon degradation by this particular species.

subject: src:scs-haima-asgard-spatial-genomes
statement: Asgard genomes were more frequently detected at the seep; candidate Gerdarchaeota encoded Wood–Ljungdahl and organic-substrate processing potential.
scope: Haima seep sediment and marine control sediments.
evidence_basis: Recover 48 MAGs across seven Asgard lineages and compare occurrence, defense genes and metabolic inventories.
locator: Publisher abstract: distribution and genomic reconstruction.
confidence_note: MAG pathways do not establish obligate autotrophy or measured chitin use; CRISPR inventories do not quantify viral protection.

subject: src:scs-scs-heimdallarchaeia-genomes
statement: The MAGs encoded diverse carbon and nitrogen pathways plus oxygen-associated genes, supporting a hypothesis of metabolically flexible Heimdallarchaeia.
scope: Four SCS seep sediment samples spanning 0–280 cm and one Western Pacific vent sample.
evidence_basis: Recover thirteen Heimdallarchaeia MAGs and compare phylogeny, carbon/nutrient genes and oxygen-related functions.
locator: Abstract; Phylogenetic status and eukaryotic signatures; Sample collection and processing.
confidence_note: Genomic oxygen/pigment genes do not demonstrate microoxic growth, photosynthesis or light-dependent metabolism in the dark seep.

subject: src:scs-mussel-seep-vent-host-microbe-response
statement: Host transcription and symbiont pathway inventories differed by ecosystem and tissue, including stress defense and sulfur/energy metabolism.
scope: Bathymodiolin mussels from SCS seeps and Southwest Indian Ocean vents, active and extinct habitats.
evidence_basis: Compare gill/digestive-gland host transcriptomes, physiological indices and symbiont metagenomes.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Different cruises, environments and hosts may covary; inferred functional compensation does not directly measure carbon transfer or survival benefit.

subject: src:scs-haima-plume-fate
statement: Observed bubbles reached near the hydrate-stability upper boundary, while dissolved methane decreased by 1–2 orders within 20–40 m above vents.
scope: Haima HM01/HMS18 seeps at 1,408–1,522-m seabed depth.
evidence_basis: Integrate bubble/plume imaging, dissolved-methane profiles, moored currents and numerical simulations.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Dissolved concentration loss is not uniquely microbial oxidation; plume height does not demonstrate surface or atmospheric methane delivery.

subject: src:scs-haima-methane-water-porewater
statement: Methane distributions varied spatially and vertically and covaried with distinct water-column and sediment geochemical variables.
scope: Haima seepage and non-seepage water/porewater profiles.
evidence_basis: Compare methane distributions with water chemistry and sediment depth, porosity and porewater constituents.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Correlations do not uniquely identify biological consumption; atmospheric-source claims require examination of the gas-exchange calculations.

subject: src:scs-formosa-tidal-methane-monitoring
statement: Gas emissions varied through time and closely tracked tidal bottom-pressure fluctuations.
scope: Formosa Ridge/Site F seep southwest of Taiwan.
evidence_basis: Monitor gas-emission intensity with ADCP, CTD and current instruments and compare bottom-pressure cycles.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: A tidal correlation supports a pressure-modulation model but does not prove hydraulic fracturing or uniform behavior across seeps.

subject: src:scs-haima-photoacoustic-methane-sensor
statement: The compact instrument measured dissolved methane during deployment; laboratory spectrometer tests reported a 0.21-ppm detection limit and approximately four-minute system response.
scope: Sensor tests and three-day deployment near Haima at 1,380-m depth.
evidence_basis: Calibrate photoacoustic/thermoelastic spectroscopy with gas extraction and test deep-water dissolved-methane measurements.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: Gas-phase spectrometer ppm cannot be treated as a dissolved-water concentration limit without extraction/calibration conversion.

subject: src:scs-haima-nutrients-chlorophyll
statement: Phosphate and chlorophyll were higher over sampled seeps than controls within an otherwise low-nutrient, low-chlorophyll setting.
scope: Haima overlying euphotic waters and control stations.
evidence_basis: Measure methane, nutrients, chlorophyll and hydrography and compare station-level associations.
locator: Abstract: study design and principal results.
confidence_note: The methane-plume nutrient-delivery mechanism was proposed but not traced; seasonal or hydrographic alternatives remain.

subject: src:scs-video-bubble-flux
statement: The observed vents differed in bubble-size distributions and inferred gas-volume flux, demonstrating strong vent-scale variability.
scope: One Haima vent and three Site F vents.
